topics.title: Java foundations
topics.description: Read Java code, follow its state and choose the result.

questions.prompt: Inside main(...), what will this score update print?
questions.explanation: score += 3 adds 3 to the current integer value 2. The result is 5, not string concatenation.

questions.prompt: Inside main(...), what is the final value printed by this loop?
questions.explanation: The loop visits 1, 2 and 3 because the condition includes 3. Their sum is 6.

questions.prompt: Which line creates an object of this class?
questions.explanation: new Quiz() calls the constructor and creates an instance. The variable round has type Quiz and refers to that instance.

questions.prompt: A quiz has 7 questions. What does this integer division print?
questions.explanation: Both operands are integers, so Java performs integer division. The fractional part is discarded, leaving 3.

questions.prompt: What value is printed after this array update?
questions.explanation: Arrays use zero-based indexes. scores[0] is 2, so the new value at index 1 is 2 + 5 = 7.

questions.prompt: A learner needs at least 4 points. What is printed for this boundary value?
questions.explanation: The >= operator includes equality. Since 4 >= 4 is true, the first branch prints Pass.

topics.title: Python essentials
topics.description: Follow Python lists, functions and loops through short examples.

questions.prompt: Which value does this list access print?
questions.explanation: List indexes start at zero. Index 1 refers to the second element, which is 4.

questions.prompt: A learner needs at least 2 points to pass. What is printed?
questions.explanation: 2 >= 2 is true. The function returns that Boolean value, and Python prints it as True.

questions.prompt: What total is printed after this loop finishes?
questions.code:
total = 0
for value in [1, 2, 3]:
    total += value
print(total)
questions.explanation: The loop adds 1, then 2, then 3 to total. The final sum is 6.

questions.prompt: How many times does this loop print the word Practice?
questions.explanation: range(1, 4) produces 1, 2 and 3. The stop value 4 is excluded, so the loop runs three times.

questions.prompt: What does this print after the new score is appended?
questions.explanation: append adds one element to the end of the list. len counts elements, so the result is 3.

questions.prompt: Which value is printed after updating this learner record?
questions.explanation: The score key initially holds 2. Adding 1 updates that value to 3; reading the same key returns 3.

topics.title: HTML & CSS
topics.description: Connect HTML structure and CSS rules to the interface they produce.

questions.prompt: Which button type submits this form when clicked?
questions.explanation: A button with type="submit" submits its associated form. type="button" has no default submit action; reset resets the form fields.

questions.prompt: Which selector targets the element with id="selected"?
questions.explanation: # selects an id. A dot selects a class, while a bare word selects elements by tag name.

questions.prompt: Assume .quiz-list is a CSS grid. What does this rule do on a narrow screen?
questions.explanation: At viewport widths of 575.98px or less, 1fr defines one grid column. Cards therefore stack in a single column.

questions.prompt: Which change connects the label to this input?
questions.explanation: A label's for attribute must match the input's id. This association gives the input an accessible name and lets clicking the label focus it.

questions.prompt: What is this card's total rendered width, including padding and borders?
questions.explanation: With border-box, the declared width already includes content, padding and borders. The outer width stays 200px (excluding margins).

questions.prompt: What color is the text in this paragraph?
questions.code: Well done
questions.explanation: Both rules match, but the id selector has greater specificity than the class selector. The text is green.
